nodes.title: GDD Game Design Document
nodes.text: > Generated from `docs/MASTER_PLAN.md` (v0.1, 2026-10-10). Owns every rule and number together with `packages/content/data/` (`@wdi/content`): `balance.json` holds the global and per-player-count values, and each role, ability, item, clue and task record holds its own (a cast time, a charge count), so no number lives in two files. A behaviour change is not done until this file changes with it.

nodes.title: GDD 1 Vision & pillars
nodes.text: A storm has closed the road and fog hides the sea. Hollowmere is cut off, Lord Vane is dead, and someone among you is still killing. Find them before the last lantern goes out. Who Did It is a 5-10 player (4 = practice; NPCs fill the seats below 4, see 3.12) hidden-role game played from a link. It crosses Among Us (tasks, bodies, emergency meetings), Mafia (hidden factions, a vote as the climax), a whodunit (physical clues with hidden attributes, a Detective who verifies them) and Hello Neighbor (houses you enter, doors that lock, hiding spots). V1 is isometric 2.5D in Phaser with pre-rendere…

nodes.title: GDD 3.1 Factions, traits and the deck
nodes.text: Factions: **Village** (blue, shield), **Cabal** (red, dagger; Killer and Accomplice know each other), **Neutral** (amber, mask). In the main mode every seat walks the world as the character of its card, so a role is public by sight, except for the three **cover roles** (Killer, Accomplice, Drifter), which always wear the look of another card of the deck (3.17). A client never receives another seat's role card, inventory, Notebook or cooldowns, and nothing it receives tells a cover look from a real one. In the quick mode (3.11) every role stays hidden. **Traits.** Each player is dealt a unique…

nodes.title: GDD 3.6 PvE
nodes.text: Players have 2 HP, regenerating 1 per 90 s; the Knife does 2. At 1 HP you are **Wounded**: 0.8x speed and a drip trail for 20 s. **Wolves** (3, forest interior loops, night): 1 damage, chase unlit players, flee any lantern or candle within 4 tiles, die to one bolt, blocked by a mended fence; a broken fence pulls one wolf into the village at night (the Cabal's reason not to mend it). The forest gate has a 6-tile safe clearing. V1 has no well fall and no bear traps; the well ladder into the cellar (`ov.well`) opens at the Large profile in V1 as a plain portal. V1.5: bear traps placed by the Ran…

nodes.text: Vision 7 tiles by day, 3.5 at night, Child -1; walking moves 3 tiles/s, running 4.5 tiles/s, and sneaking (Shift) is silent at 60% of walking speed. A door is usable from 1.5 tiles of its tile centre, the same reach as the other verbs; the body's collision box is a 0.5-tile square under the feet (WORLD 4.2). Noise radii in tiles: walk 2, run 6, door 4, kill scream 8, rag 4, skeleton key 5, crowbar 10, bolt 10, lockpick 5, hide 2, burst out 6, one-way drop 9, the barn goat 4, a Wisp rattle 2; noise renders as a screen-edge pulse with a direction arrow and a log line, crossing a portal at 50% r…

nodes.title: GDD 3.8 Meetings, voting and win conditions
nodes.text: - **Village** wins when all Cabal are dead or ejected, tasks reach 100%, or the Final Night vote ejects a Cabal member. - **Cabal** wins at parity (living Cabal >= living Village; Thief counts as Village, Drifter as nobody) at 6+ players; at 4-5 when living Village <= 1; or when the Final Night vote ejects nobody or a non-Cabal player. - **Drifter** wins alone when ejected, and the match goes on. (M5a) The end screen lists an ejected Drifter among the winners (`gameOver.alsoWon`) whichever faction then wins; a Drifter who is killed, poisoned or shot loses. nodes.title: GDD 3.18 Cinematics and music
nodes.text: Round 6 (ROADMAP M5c). Cutscenes are data (`packages/content/data/cutscenes/`) played in-engine: the opening of a map runs inside grace, which `phases.openingS` lengthens for it, and adds no phase; a death plays the cutscene of its cause before the ghost handoff; every cutscene can be skipped, and reduce-motion turns its camera moves into cuts. nodes.text: Round 6 (ROADMAP M5d). nodes.text: Round 7 (ROADMAP R7). nodes.text: **Start and role card (2:00-2:23).** The server deals roles and traits, locks the room and sends each client its private card. The card shows: faction stripe and icon, role name, your character with your traits and the line "You walk as the Baker: Tall / Green scarf / Bowler hat" (a cover role picks the look here instead, 3.17), the deck list, a one-line goal, up to 3 ability rows with key and cooldown, the inventory strip, 2-3 sentences of card text, a Beware line, and for Cabal the teammate names. It holds 20 s; Ready dismisses it; Tab reopens it; a HUD chip (icon + goal) stays top-left.

Outside the lane you can see the forest gate and, beyond the gate, the forest scene with the cave mouth.

nodes.text: **First body (4:30).** Night falls (10 s vignette, then a 100 s night with a 3.5-tile light radius). Somewhere a scream pulses at your screen edge with a direction arrow and a log line "A scream from the north". The Killer carries Blood for 60 s and walks to the well to wash. You find the body in the apothecary loft: E reports it; everyone teleports to the square; the body stays where it was.

nodes.title: WORLD World Bible and Level Design
nodes.text: > Generated from `docs/MASTER_PLAN.md` (v0.1, 2026-10-10). Geography, scene ids, portal ids, lore and lighting. Numbers that affect play live in `GDD.md`.

nodes.title: WORLD 4.1 Setting
nodes.text: **Hollowmere**, a fog-bound harbour hamlet on a northern coast, autumn 1931. The storm closed the only road; the fog hides the sea. Lord Aldous Vane, owner of the shuttered tin mine, died three nights ago and his will names "whoever remains when the last lantern goes out". The flooded lowest gallery leaks "mere-rot" into the marsh, which makes the wolves bold and wakes something in the sea cave (the Beast, V2). Tone: toon-noir, chunky villagers in trench coats and wool caps, wet cobbles, amber lantern light against slate-blue dusk. Landmark NPCs (Mrs Grieves the tavern keeper, Old Fennick at…

nodes.title: WORLD 4.2 Metrics
nodes.text: `TILE_PX = 64` and 1 tile = 1 m. Every rule, radius, collision box and id lives on this square grid, on the server and in the data. A player's collision box is a 0.5-tile square under the feet (`metrics.json`). All radii in rules are in tiles and live in `@wdi/shared/constants.ts`. Interiors are at least 12x9 tiles (the loft and bedroom rooms), with camera follow and no whole-room fit. Every size is in 4.3, 4.10 and `scenes/*.json`. (M5a) **The client draws this grid in 2:1 dimetric isometric projection**, seen from the south-east (GDD 3.13, SPRITES 10): - A tile is a 128 x 64 px diamond. The…

nodes.title: WORLD 4.10 Blackpine
nodes.text: **Blackpine** is the Vane Timber and Tin Company's camp in the pine valley above Hollowmere, the same autumn of 1931. nodes.title: UI UI design system
nodes.text: The DOM overlay's look: what every screen the player meets shares, from the Landing buttons to the dark loft of the quick mode. It is implemented in `apps/client/src/ui/theme/` (tokens and component classes, one import per screen), drawn in `apps/client/public/assets/ui/` (frames, marks, glyphs) and previewed in `apps/client/public/theme-preview.html` and `apps/client/public/mockups/`. Numbers in this document that are rules of play (the 12 s card hold, the 60 s discussion, the 4 to 10 players) are `docs/GDD.md`'s; this document only says how they look. The scale in 4 and 5 is machine-readabl…

nodes.title: UI 1 Principles
nodes.text: 1. **Readable at 390 px wide and at 200% UI scale.** Every screen is a single column on a phone; nothing is narrower than one thumb. Type is in `rem`, strokes and spacing in `px`, so browser zoom scales the words and keeps the ink crisp. Nothing is set below 12 px. 2. **Night chrome, paper controls.** The page is `ink`, panels are `slate`, and everything the player can touch is `bone` paper with a 2 px `ink` stroke. The eye learns in one screen that paper is live. 3. **One saturated accent per element.** A button is mustard or it is paper; a chip has one colour; a card has one faction. Satura…

nodes.title: UI 2 Palette
nodes.text: The ten tokens of `packages/content/data/palette.json` (docs/ASSETS.md 6.1) and its five-colour `night` set (round 7, below) are the only colours. CSS exposes each as `--wdi-<name>` and as `--wdi-<name>-rgb` so an alpha variant is written `rgb(var(--wdi-bone-rgb) / 0.72)` and no new hex is ever born. The night roles: | Role token | Palette | Used for | |---|---|---| | `--wdi-bg` | ink | page, world scrim, wells (timers, code boxes, chat log) | | `--wdi-surface` | slate | panels, dialogs, the meeting board, the card back | | `--wdi-paper` | bone (+ grain) | cards, buttons, inputs, chips, toast…

nodes.title: UI 3 Type
nodes.text: Oswald for display (titles, buttons, names, codes, chips: uppercase, tracked) and Inter for text (body, hints, inputs, chat). Both are self-hosted variable fonts under the OFL (`apps/client/src/assets/fonts/`, texts in `LICENSES/fonts/`); `tokens.css` declares them. **The pixel faces (round 7, 7B, DECISIONS A106).** The night theme adds Press Start 2P (`--wdi-font-pixel-display`, one weight) and Pixelify Sans (`--wdi-font-pixel-text`, variable 400 to 700), both OFL, self-hosted from Fontsource 5.3.0 as Latin woff2 (12.2 and 11.7 KiB, about 24 KiB together, bundled with the stylesheet and fetc…

nodes.title: UI 4 Space, radius, stroke, grid
nodes.text: Space on a 4 px base: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48 (`--wdi-space-1` to `-7`). Panels pad 24 (16 on phones); rows are at least 44 px tall (`--wdi-touch`, the hit target); gaps inside a component are 8, between components 12, between sections 24. Radius: 2 (stroke corners, timer bars), 6 (chips, inputs, keycaps), 10 (buttons, rows, toasts), 16 (panels, dialogs), 20 (reserved for the card when it has no frame), pill for the HUD chip and clock. The framed card is rectangular; its outer stroke corners are 2 px. Stroke: 2 px (`palette.rules.uiStrokePx`), round caps and joins, `ink`. Icons, marks and fr…

nodes.title: UI 5 Ink stroke and paper fill
nodes.text: Paper is `bone` under a grain of `ink` noise at 10% or less (`--wdi-paper-grain`, an inline SVG turbulence; no colour of its own). Every paper element has the 2 px ink stroke; on paper, a divider is ink at 18% and a sunken field has a 2 px ink inner shadow at the top. On dark surfaces the stroke is `ink` too (a panel edge against the page reads as a dark gap plus a 1 px bone hairline inset), and dividers are the hairline. Ink-stroked glyphs vanish on slate, so on a dark surface an icon sits on a paper disc (`.wdi-icon-disc`, 36 or 48 px), as `docs/SPRITES.md` 9 requires. The faction icons on…

nodes.title: UI 6 Components
nodes.text: **Buttons** (`.wdi-btn`). Oswald caps at 18 px, 44 px tall, 8/16 padding, radius 10, the ink stroke, a slate shadow. Variants: `--primary` (mustard, ink text, the one per screen), default (paper), `--ghost` (transparent, bone text, hairline stroke, for Leave and Not yet), `--danger` (blood, bone text, for the eject vote). Sizes `--sm` 36 px, `--lg` 56 px, `--icon` square, `--block`. States: hover lifts 1 px and deepens the shadow; active sinks 1 px with no shadow; `:disabled` and `aria-disabled` fade to 50% with a not-allowed cursor (the "Waking the village..." state is a disabled primary); `…

nodes.title: UI 7 The role card
nodes.text: The card is the one place the faction shows. Structure, top to bottom (`.wdi-card`): 1. **Stripe** (`__stripe`): the faction colour, the faction icon on a bone circle, the faction word. Village moon with ink text, Cabal blood with bone text, Neutral mustard with ink text. 2. **Title** (`__title`): the role name, display-lg, centred. 3. **Look** (`__look`): "You look like" and the three trait icons with their labels. 4. **Goal** (`__goal`): one line, text-lg semibold, between two ink rules. 5. **Abilities** (`__ability`): up to three rows of keycap, name, cooldown. 6. **Inventory** (`__invento…

nodes.title: UI 8 Shadows and glows
nodes.text: `--wdi-shadow-1` (2/6 slate 55%) for buttons and chips at rest, `-2` (8/24 slate 70%) for panels and toasts, `-3` (18/48 slate 85%) for the card. Glows are a 1 px ring plus a 16 to 24 px blur of the accent at 25 to 50%: `--wdi-glow-moon` for night and the loft, `-interact` for a selection, `-hazard` for a cue. Never a black shadow.

nodes.title: ARCHITECTURE 5.11 Security
nodes.text: Every action validated server-side (range, phase, cooldown, ownership, alive, busy). `maxMessagesPerSecond = 100` as a hard cap; per-type token buckets drop rather than disconnect; disconnect only after 3 overflows in 10 s. Names 2-16 characters, server-side profanity list (M7). Chat channels derived from alive status and role; the client's channel field is ignored. Debug handlers register only with `WDI_DEBUG=1` and never in production; a CI test asserts `debug.roles` is absent from a production build. Seeds sent to clients drive cosmetics only. `onLeave` during play spawns a "vanished" body…

nodes.title: SPRITES 1 Cells, scale and directions
nodes.text: - Character cells are **128 px displayed cells, packed at 64 px** (10.3). One tile is 64 px = 1 m (`TILE_PX`, `WORLD.md` 4.2). A standing 1.7 m villager is about 100 px tall in the cell. - Animations play at **12 fps**. The rig renders the source clip with `frame_step` so the output is 12 fps whatever the clip's scene rate. - Height traits are not separate art: the client scales the sprite by the GDD 3.1 factor, anchored at the feet pivot. - Eight directions, clockwise from screen up; the atlas `<dir>` is screen frame, data and wire directions are world frame (10.4). nodes.title: SPRITES 10.2 The projection
nodes.text: **Formulas.** World px (wx, wy) to screen px (sx, sy), and back: ``` sx = wx - wy wx = sy + sx / 2 sy = (wx + wy) / 2 wy = sy - sx / 2 ``` **What follows from them:** - **A tile is a 128 x 64 diamond.** Tile (tx, ty) has its top vertex at ((tx - ty)·64, (tx + ty)·32) and its centre at ((tx - ty)·64, (tx + ty + 1)·32). - **Area is kept.** The determinant is 1: a world tile is 4096 px² and so is its diamond. A camera zoom therefore shows as many tiles as it did before. - **World directions on screen.** A world unit vector goes to: - north -> (1, -½), the upper right; - east -> (1, ½), the lower…

Screen right is world north-east, and screen up is world north-west. - Built by `tools/blender/build_rig.py` beside the old cameras. `CAMERA_TILT_DEG` becomes 60, and a `CAMERA_YAW_DEG = 45` joins it in `rig_common.py`. - The lights stay parented to the camera, unchanged: key from screen-left at azimuth 225°, the moon fill, no cast shadows. **Scale.** - Every fram…

nodes.title: SPRITES 10.8 Input
nodes.text: The key vector stays screen-axis (`keyVector`: W up, D right). It is turned into the world by **`keysToWorld`**, a -45° rotation: - each single key walks straight along a screen axis: W is world north-west, D is world north-east; - two keys walk along the grid: W+D is world north. A touch stick's offset goes through **`stickToWorld`**, the exact inverse projection: the character walks where the thumb points on the screen. Keys and stick are converted separately and then summed. The server normalises the vector (`Movement.ts`), so speed in tiles per second is unchanged. Mock feeds and bots alr…

nodes.text: **Zoom** = clamp(floor(height / (`iso.viewTilesHigh`·64) / `iso.zoomStep`)·`zoomStep`, 0.5, 2). nodes.title: SPRITES 10.10 The vision ellipse
nodes.text: Your light is centred on your feet (screen), with radius `radiusEllipse(r)·zoom`: - r = `balance.vision` lerped from `dayTiles` to `nightTiles` by `Lighting.darkness` (dusk and dawn ease); - r = `nightTiles` in a dark scene, whatever the phase. The vision ellipse is the only light the server could ever check (M5b). In M5a it is a picture.

nodes.title: ROADMAP 7.6 Workflow
nodes.text: `main` is always deployable and protected by CI. One branch per milestone task (`m4a/clues-and-lenses`), one AI session per branch scoped to a single task prompt from `ROADMAP.md`, PRs under 400 lines with tests for rules changes and a GDD note when behaviour changes. Squash-merge; tag `v0.<milestone>.<n>` at milestone exit. `pnpm docs:balance` regenerates `BALANCE.md` from `balance.json` and the PR template has a "docs updated" checkbox; there is no CI grep gate, no changelog automation and no preview deployments until a second contributor exists. Sessions never upgrade dependencies.

nodes.title: MASTER_PLAN 1 Vision & pillars
nodes.text: A storm has closed the road and fog hides the sea. Hollowmere is cut off, Lord Vane is dead, and someone among you is still killing. Find them before the last lantern goes out. nodes.title: MASTER_PLAN 5.7 Scene sync
nodes.text: `act.enterPortal` validates distance, lock state, profile and phase, sets `sceneId`, position and the 0.6 s transit, swaps `scenes` view entries and other players' `presence`, and broadcasts a door `swing` plus a noise event. Meetings run the same transition path for every player (busy, input clear, `sceneEnter` to a spread spawn). After a meeting everyone stays at the square; hiding spots are emptied; bodies stay. nodes.title: MASTER_PLAN 7.6 Workflow
nodes.text: `main` is always deployable and protected by CI. One branch per milestone task (`m4a/clues-and-lenses`), one AI session per branch scoped to a single task prompt from `ROADMAP.md`, PRs under 400 lines with tests for rules changes and a GDD note when behaviour changes. Squash-merge; tag `v0.<milestone>.<n>` at milestone exit. `pnpm docs:balance` regenerates `BALANCE.md` from `balance.json` and the PR template has a "docs updated" checkbox; there is no CI grep gate, no changelog automation and no preview deployments until a second contributor exists. Sessions never upgrade dependencies.

nodes.title: CLAUDE What this repo is
nodes.text: A browser multiplayer hidden-role game for 4 to 10 players: a static Phaser client on GitHub Pages and an authoritative Colyseus server. V1 is isometric 2.5D (since round 5, DECISIONS A49) with pre-rendered and generated sprites; V2 is first-person 3D on the same server, rules and world data. It also ships a short quick mode, One Night Ultimate Baguette (length in `GDD.md` 3.11). Implementation started 2026-10-10 in four parallel sessions; `docs/SESSIONS.md` says which paths each session owns. Until their PRs merge, `docs/` and the root scaffold are the whole project.

nodes.title: round5/art-plan 9.2 What the code decides
nodes.text: These are fixed so that no session has to guess: - **Images.** `Rgba` is `bleed.ts`'s straight 8-bit RGBA (`Uint8Array`). PNG input and output go through `bleed.ts`'s `decodePng` and `encodePng`, which are deterministic and never premultiply. WebP goes through `@napi-rs/canvas` `encode('webp', quality)`. At 100 it is lossless, and the test decodes the file and compares every pixel. - **Alpha cut.** Alpha at or above `pixel.alphaCut` × 255 (128 and up) becomes 255. Transparent pixels become 0, 0, 0, 0. - **Snap.** Squared Euclidean distance in OKLab to the 64 colours. An exact tie goes to the…

nodes.title: round5/owner-brief The ONUB spec
nodes.text: In One Night Ultimate Baguette, every player experiences a two-part gameplay loop: first, they physically visit one of the 4 Main Kitchen Stations during the Evening Prep (Among Us task phase), and second, they execute their secret Brigade Role Action from their personal station during the Night Phase (One Night Werewolf manipulation phase). Here is exactly what the player does in each scene, broken down by station and role.

nodes.title: round5/owner-brief PART 1 The 4 Physical Prep Stations (Evening Task Phase)
nodes.text: Before the lights go out, every player secretly chooses one of the four main rooms to visit by placing that Location Card face-down in front of them, then contributes one card to that room's specific Prep Pile.

nodes.title: round5/owner-brief PART 1.1 La Chambre Froide (The Walk-In Fridge)
nodes.text: * In-World Action: You are checking temperatures, harvesting wild yeast, and pulling cold butter and milk crates from the frosted shelves. * Player Mechanic: * Loyal Bakers add Pure Dairy & Active Yeast cards into the Fridge Prep Pile. * Saboteurs slip Spoiled Milk or Unpasteurized Mold into the pile, or flip the thermostat switch (forcing one random card from the Fridge pile to be discarded blindly). * The Alibi Risk: Because the floor is covered in frost, anyone who visits the Walk-In Fridge leaves "chilled" footprints—if the Fridge is sabotaged, anyone claiming they were here immediately b…

nodes.title: round5/owner-brief PART 1.2 Le Pétrin (The Industrial Mixer)
nodes.text: * In-World Action: You are hauling heavy sacks of Farine (flour), pouring buckets of water, and running the giant spiral dough hook. * Player Mechanic: * Loyal Bakers play T55 Flour and Sea Salt cards into the Mixer Bowl pile. * Saboteurs dump Sawdust, Plaster, or Floor Sweepings into the mixer. * The Alibi Risk: The Mixer requires at least two ingredient cards to run. If only one person visits Le Pétrin, the dough is under-mixed, automatically triggering a caution flag in the morning.

nodes.title: round5/owner-brief PART 1.3 La Chambre de Pousse (The Proofing Drawer)
nodes.text: * In-World Action: You are sliding wooden banneton baskets of shaped dough into the warm, humid glass cabinets and monitoring the fermentation dials. * Player Mechanic: * Loyal Bakers play Warm Steam and Time cards. * Saboteurs play Cold Draft or Over-Proofing cards to collapse the dough. * Station Perk: Because the Proofing Drawer has glass doors and bright warm bulbs, if zero Sabotage cards are played here, the players who visited this station get to collectively peek at one unused Location Card from the center Pantry before the Night Phase begins.

nodes.title: round5/owner-brief PART 1.4 Le Four à Pain (The Brick Oven)
nodes.text: * In-World Action: You are stoking the wood fire, wielding the long wooden peel, and injecting steam for the coup de buée (the crispy crust). * Player Mechanic: * Loyal Bakers play Oak Firewood and Steam Injection cards. * Saboteurs play Charcoal Ash or Wet Wood to choke the heat. * The High Stakes: Sabotage cards played at the Brick Oven count double toward ruining the Mother Dough, making it the hottest battleground for accusations during the Morning Rush.

nodes.title: round5/owner-brief PART 2 The Role Scenes (Night Phase Actions)
nodes.text: Once the Prep Piles are revealed (showing where sabotage happened, but not who did it), the lights go out. The narrator calls each role in order. Here is what you do when your station is called:

nodes.title: round5/owner-brief PART 2.1 The Saboteurs' Cellar (Le Champignon & Le Levain)
nodes.text: * Le Champignon (The Mold Spore): * In-Scene Action: You crawl out from behind the glowing green damp bricks and sacks of spoiled flour. * Tabletop Action: Open your eyes and look around for other Mold Spores. If you are the only Spore among the players, you may secretly look at one center Pantry Role Card so you can safely bluff as that role in the morning. * Le Levain (The Sourdough Starter): * In-Scene Action: Your giant glass fermentation jar bubbles over in the candlelight, feeding the spores. * Tabletop Action: Keep your eyes closed while the Spores stick their thumbs up. You open your…

nodes.title: round5/owner-brief PART 2.2 The Sub-Basement Vent (Le Rat de Cave & L'Apprenti)
nodes.text: * L'Apprenti (The Unpaid Intern): * In-Scene Action: Exhausted by a 16-hour shift on a wooden stool, you snoop through the shift logs by a single hanging bulb. * Tabletop Action: Wake up after the Spores and peek at one other player's Location Card. When morning comes, you can whisper or signal to your fellow Saboteurs which room is safe to claim as an alibi. * Le Rat de Cave (The Cellar Rat): * In-Scene Action: You pry open the iron floor grate and vent out of the crime scene, leaving a trail of flour footprints leading to someone else's station. * Tabletop Action: Swap your own Location Car…

nodes.title: round5/owner-brief PART 2.3 The Shaping Bench (Le Boulanger — Head Baker)
nodes.text: * In-Scene Action: You slam the heavy Cast Iron Cloche down onto the floured wooden table to protect your prized dough from tampering. * Tabletop Action: Wake up first and place the physical Iron Cloche Token on top of any player's Role Card or Location Card (including your own). For the rest of the night, no other role can peek at or swap that card.

nodes.title: round5/owner-brief PART 2.4 The Command Desk (Le Chef de Cuisine & Le Sous-Chef)
nodes.text: * Le Chef de Cuisine (Executive Chef): * In-Scene Action: Sitting under the green banker's lamp with your magnifying glass, you audit the kitchen's personnel files and blueprints. * Tabletop Action: Wake up and either peek at one other player's Role Card OR peek at two Role Cards in the center Pantry. * Le Sous-Chef (Second-in-Command): * In-Scene Action: You ringside the brass desk bell and reassign kitchen staff mid-shift to cover a station. * Tabletop Action: Wake up and swap your Role Card with another player's Role Card, then look at your new card. (Warning: If you steal a Mold Spore car…

nodes.title: round5/owner-brief PART 2.5 The Expediter's Pass (L'Aboyeur)
nodes.text: * In-Scene Action: Standing under the red heat lamps, you check the order tickets against the grainy green-tinted CRT security monitor watching the four kitchen rooms. * Tabletop Action: Wake up and look at two different players' Location Cards. You don't know what role they are, but you know with 100% certainty which stations they actually visited during the Prep Phase—allowing you to instantly catch anyone lying about their room alibi.

nodes.title: round5/owner-brief PART 2.6 The Lamination Room (Le Tourrier — Dough Sheeter)
nodes.text: * In-Scene Action: You feed blocks of Beurre (butter) and dough back and forth through the heavy mechanical rollers, folding an unused recipe into the active lineup. * Tabletop Action: Wake up and look at one center Pantry Role Card. You must then swap that Pantry card with any player's Role Card (even your own), completely changing who holds that role at the table.

nodes.title: round5/owner-brief PART 2.7 The Cold Pantry (Le Garde Manger)
nodes.text: * In-Scene Action: Surrounded by hanging cured meats, wheels of cheese, and a few too many spilled glasses of cooking wine, you stumble out of the pantry and forget what station you were assigned to. * Tabletop Action: Wake up and swap your own Role Card with a center Pantry Role Card without looking at it. You enter the Morning Rush having no idea if you are still a Loyal Baker or if you accidentally just became a Mold Spore.

nodes.title: round5/owner-brief PART 2.8 The Dish Pit (Le Plongeur — The Dishwasher)
nodes.text: * In-Scene Action: Blinded by overflowing soapsuds, steam, and "Wet Floor" cones, you frantically grab stacks of dirty sheet pans and return them to the wrong stations. * Tabletop Action: Wake up and blindly swap two other players' Role Cards OR two other players' Location Cards. You create pure deduction chaos—forcing players to realize in the morning that their identities or alibis have been switched behind their backs.

nodes.title: round5/owner-brief Overview (second attachment)
nodes.text: One Night Ultimate Baguette is a fast-paced social deduction game (10–15 minutes) that combines the room-based tasks and alibis of Among Us with the single-night card swapping of One Night Ultimate Werewolf. You and your friends are French bakers working the graveyard shift before the Paris Bake-Off. Hidden among you are Mold Spores trying to ruin the Mother Dough. There are no player eliminations during the game—everyone plays until the timer runs out, and the entire game comes down to a single explosive 5-minute argument and one final vote.

nodes.title: round5/owner-brief The Setup: Two Cards Per Player
nodes.text: Unlike normal Werewolf where you only have an identity, every player in this game manages two secret cards face-down in front of them: * Your Role Card (Who you are): Your job in the kitchen brigade (e.g., Mold Spore, Chef de Cuisine, Sous-Chef, Dishwasher). Three extra Role Cards are placed face-down in the center of the table (The Pantry). * Your Location Card (Where you worked): Which of the 4 physical kitchen stations you visit during the shift (Walk-In Fridge, Industrial Mixer, Proofing Drawer, or Brick Oven).

nodes.title: round5/owner-brief Phase 1: The Evening Prep (The Among Us Phase)
nodes.text: Before anyone closes their eyes, everyone completes a 60-second simultaneous task phase: * Pick a Room: Every player secretly selects one of the 4 Location Cards and places it face-down in front of them. * Add to the Dough: Players secretly contribute one Ingredient Card from their hand into the face-down "Prep Pile" of the room they chose. * Loyal Bakers must play good ingredients (Flour, Water, Yeast, Steam). * Mold Spores can play Sabotage Cards (Sawdust, Spoiled Milk, Bleach)—or play good ingredients to blend in. * Reveal the Crime Scenes: Each room's Prep Pile is shuffled and flipped fac…

nodes.title: round5/owner-brief Phase 2: The Baking Cycle (The One Night Werewolf Phase)
nodes.text: Everyone closes their eyes. A dramatic French narrator (via an app or moderator) calls out roles one by one to wake up and tamper with the cards on the table in total silence. Because players have both a Role Card and a Location Card, night actions mess with both your identity and your alibi: * The Saboteurs (Mold Spores, Sourdough Starter, Cellar Rat): Wake up to see who their fellow traitors are, peek at unpicked center cards to fake claims, or "vent" by swapping their Location Card with another room so they aren't caught at a sabotaged station. * The Investigators (Chef de Cuisine, Expedit…

nodes.title: round5/owner-brief Phase 3: The Morning Rush (5-Minute Emergency Meeting)
nodes.text: Everyone opens their eyes. Rule #1: You are NOT allowed to look at your Role Card or Location Card anymore. A 5-minute timer starts, and everyone argues at once to figure out two puzzles before time runs out: * Who sabotaged the stations during Phase 1? ("Three of us claim we went to the Brick Oven, and there's Charcoal Ash in the pile! One of us is lying!") * Whose cards got swapped during Phase 2? * The Twist: You always play for the team of the Role Card currently sitting in front of you, not the card you started with! * Example: If you started the game as a Mold Spore and sabotaged the Wa…

nodes.title: round5/owner-brief Phase 4: The Final Bake (Voting & Winning)
nodes.text: When the 5-minute timer rings, everyone counts down "Un, deux, trois—CRUST!" and points at one player to throw into the Brick Oven. The player with the most votes flips their cards over. * Team Loyal Baker Wins: If at least one player currently holding a Mold Spore card is voted into the oven. (If all Mold Spore cards ended up in the center Pantry, Bakers win by pointing at the center of the table). * Team Mold Spore Wins: If no Mold Spores are voted out—OR if the Saboteurs successfully slipped 3+ Sabotage weight into the Prep Piles during Phase 1 (the baguette is ruined no matter who gets vo…

nodes.title: round5/world 8.2 cave_gallery: The Flooded Gallery
nodes.text: **The Flooded Gallery** is Vane's lowest tin gallery, flooded and leaking mere-rot into the fen. It is dark; its light comes from the mere-rot on the water, moss, one dropped miner's lamp and the daylight down the sinkhole shaft. Points of interest: - **The entry passage** (x 19-21) runs up from `cg.upper` into **the junction** (x 14-26, y 14-20), which holds a rat run. - **The flooded stope** (west, x 3-13, y 4-16): deep water with shallow margins, crossed by a plank walkway along y 10. The mere-rot glows teal on it in three places. The sump (`cg.sump`, a body spot) is at its south margin. -…

nodes.title: round5/world 8.3 bp_camp: Blackpine Camp
nodes.text: **Blackpine Camp** is the hub. Points of interest: - **The edges.** The north edge is the hill: a cliff 4 tiles deep, with the adit (`bc.adit`) cut into it and tram rails running down to the ore bin (`bc.ore_bin`, a hiding spot). nodes.title: round6/auto-admin Round-6 contract: the admin auto-mode
nodes.text: The owner's request: "a special admin section that only I can access where I can play the game on auto mode with all the NPC roles playing out on multi screens at 10x speed for me to check the game for errors and bugs." nodes.title: round6/auto-admin 7 The GitHub login (6C)
nodes.text: **Flow.** `GET /auth/github/login` -> 302 to GitHub's authorize URL (`scope=read:user`, a signed stateless `state` = `base64url(nonce.issuedAt) + '.' + HMAC`) -> `GET /auth/github/callback?code&state` -> verify the state (HMAC with `timingSafeEqual`, issued under 10 minutes ago) -> `fetch` the access token -> `fetch https://api.github.com/user` -> `login.toLowerCase()` in the allowlist -> `signAdminToken({ sub: login, id, exp })` -> 302 to `${WDI_ADMIN_CLIENT_URL}#/admin?token=...`. The client moves the token into `sessionStorage['wdi:adminToken']` and scrubs the hash with `setRoute`. No cook…

nodes.text: The Frontier Company Town HollowMere is a claustrophobic, superstitious railroad town controlled by ruthless Railroad Barons. The Scene Graph & Player-Count Profiles HollowMere scales dynamically across Small (4–6 players), Medium (7–8 players), and Large (9–10 players) profiles using district gates (gates in overworld.json), ensuring the social density remains tight while every entered building features at least two co…

nodes.title: round7/parties 1 The rule in one paragraph

nodes.title: round7/parties 5 What this design accepts and records
nodes.text: - A profile code is sent by the client and never proven, so a device that knows a friend's code sees the private parties that friend was invited to. The game is played among friends; the leader sees who joins and the M7 kick and ban stay the remedy. Recorded as the open column of A104. - A profile lives on one device. Moving it is copying the code and name by hand; no account, no sync, no server storage this round. - Nothing here touches role secrecy: the listing stops at the lobby, and a profile code is as public as a name.

nodes.title: guides/ADMIN_GUIDE Admin guide: auto-mode
nodes.text: The owner-only page runs a match in which every seat is an NPC, watched from a god view at up to ten times speed, with the match invariants checked as it runs. It exists to find bugs. The contract is [`docs/round6/auto-admin.md`](../round6/auto-admin.md); the design is [`docs/GDD.md`](../GDD.md) 3.19.

nodes.title: guides/ADMIN_GUIDE Turning it on
nodes.text: The admin room and its login routes exist only when the server has the GitHub login configured. `README.md` lists the six `WDI_ADMIN_*` variables: the flag, the GitHub OAuth app's client id and secret, the allowlist of GitHub logins, a signing secret and the client URL. Without them a `party` room never accepts an admin message and the `#/admin` route refuses. 1. Create a GitHub OAuth app whose callback URL is `https://<server host>/auth/github/callback`. 2. Set the variables on the server (Railway: Variables tab) and redeploy. 3. Open `https://<server host>/auth/github/login`. GitHub asks yo…

nodes.title: guides/ADMIN_GUIDE The page
nodes.text: - **Setup**: map, mode, seat count, NPC difficulty, the quick mode's deck, and optionally the seed words. **Start** needs no leader and no human. - **Clock**: 1x, 2x, 5x, 10x, pause and single step. Every timer in the game counts ticks, so phase lengths, cooldowns and countdowns keep their meaning at any speed. When the server cannot keep up it runs fewer ticks and reports the speed it reached; no tick is skipped. - **Viewports**: one per occupied scene, up to six on a grid; extra scenes queue in the inspector. "Follow seat" collapses to one viewport. - **Seat inspector**: role, cover, invent…

nodes.title: guides/ADMIN_GUIDE Replaying a failure
nodes.text: An auto match fixes the seed words of every random stream and the seat ids before Start, so the same words replay the same match tick for tick. Paste the words from a failure line into Setup to watch it again.

nodes.title: guides/ADMIN_GUIDE The headless runner
nodes.text: ``` pnpm auto -- --matches 20 --seed 7 --map blackpine --mode main --difficulty hard --json ``` One line per match (winner, ticks, rounds, invariant failures); a failure prints the seed words and seat ids; exit code 1 on any failure. The weekly soak workflow runs it too.

nodes.title: guides/HOST_GUIDE Host guide
nodes.text: How to get a party into a match, and what to do when something sticks. Player counts, the NPC fill and the lobby settings are in [`docs/GDD.md`](../GDD.md) 2, 3.9 and 3.12.

nodes.title: guides/HOST_GUIDE Making a party
nodes.text: 1. Open [https://groot99-droid.github.io/Who-Did-It/](https://groot99-droid.github.io/Who-Did-It/). 2. Type a name and press **Create Party**. You are the leader. 3. The lobby shows a short party code and **Copy invite link**. Send the link or the code. Friends who open the link find the code prefilled; everyone else presses **Join Party** and types it. 4. Watch the roster fill. Each player presses **Ready**. 5. Press **Start**. If someone is not Ready you get a confirm dialog listing them. Roles are dealt at once and nobody can join after this. The game is best with six to eight players and…

nodes.title: guides/HOST_GUIDE Lobby settings
nodes.text: - **Mode**: Who Did It (the main mode, with the village) or One Night Ultimate Baguette (the quick mode, no walking). See [Quick mode](QUICK_MODE.md). - **Map**: Hollowmere or Blackpine (main mode only). - **Add NPC / Remove NPC** and **NPC difficulty**: fill or thin the table with bots. - **Art style** (landing page): 8-bit or low poly, per player, changed at any time. - **Sound** (gear): music, effects and mute, per player. After game over the party returns to the lobby with the same code and seats, so a second round is one press of Start.

nodes.title: guides/HOST_GUIDE When something sticks
nodes.text: | Symptom | What is happening | | ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | The buttons read "Waking the village..." | The server is starting up. Wait a few seconds; the buttons go live on their own. | | "Party not found" on Join | Check the code: it never uses 0, O, 1 or I. The party may already have started, which locks it. | | A player dropped | They can reopen the link within about a minute and resume the same role. After that…

nodes.title: guides/HOST_GUIDE Running your own server
nodes.text: The client is a static page; the server is a Colyseus app. `README.md` lists the environment variables and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` 5 the deployment. The client reads the server address from `apps/client/.env.production` at build time, or from the `VITE_SERVER_URL` Actions variable.

nodes.title: guides/HOW_TO_PLAY How to play Who Did It
nodes.text: A hidden-role whodunit for a party of friends in a browser. Most of you are villagers; a few are the Cabal, who kill after dark and lie about it. Find the bodies, read the clues, argue, and vote. The numbers (phase lengths, light radius, cooldowns, win thresholds) are in [`docs/GDD.md`](../GDD.md), sections 2, 3.3 and 3.8.

nodes.title: guides/HOW_TO_PLAY Getting in
nodes.text: 1. Open the game link your host sent you, or go to the game page and press **Join Party**. 2. Type a name and the party code (the link prefills it). You land in the lobby. 3. Press **Ready**. When the leader presses **Start**, roles are dealt and the party locks. Headphones help: screams, doors and footsteps come with a direction.

nodes.title: guides/HOW_TO_PLAY Controls
nodes.text: | Action | Keyboard | Touch | | ------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------- | | Move | WASD or the arrow keys | drag on the left half | | Sneak (quiet, slower) | hold Shift | **Sneak** | | Run (louder) | Space | **Run** | | Use a door, bell or body | E | **Use** | | Collect a clue | hold E until the ring fills | hold **Use** | | Role ability | Q, R or F, as the card shows | **Act** | | Role card | Tab | the chip top-left | | Notebook | N | the button beside the chip | | Skip a cutscene | Esc or the Skip button | tap Skip | A prompt near your characte…

nodes.title: guides/HOW_TO_PLAY Your role card
nodes.text: The card shows your faction stripe, your role, the character you walk as, your goal in one line, your abilities with their keys, and a **Beware** line. Cabal members also see their teammates. Read it during the role reveal; press Tab to open it again at any time. Everyone in the main mode walks as their card's character, so the Vicar looks like the Vicar. The exceptions are the **cover roles** (the Killer, the Accomplice and the Drifter), who pick another card's look and wear it all match. A look is a claim, not proof: two players in the same look means one of them is a cover. GDD 3.17 has th…

nodes.title: guides/HOW_TO_PLAY The loop of a match
nodes.text: - **Grace.** Everyone spawns around the hub. Nobody can be killed. A glowing clue by the well teaches the collect verb. The map's opening cinematic plays over this; skip it with Esc. - **Day.** Free roam in good light. Gather resources, craft, take quests, do tasks at the stations. The bell on the square calls a meeting, once per player. - **Dusk.** "Night falls." The Knife and the night powers wake. If a body has gone unreported, or someone has not been seen for a whole cycle, a roll-call meeting opens instead. - **Night.** Short sight, wolves in the woods, the hunt. A scream pulses at your…

nodes.title: guides/HOW_TO_PLAY Clues and the Notebook
nodes.text: Bodies, footprints, dropped items and traces are clues. Hold E on a glowing one to collect it into your Notebook, which records what it says about the culprit's traits ("long stride: Tall"). A **Verified** entry (the Detective's, or one the board confirms) carries more weight in a meeting than a **Claimed** one. The meeting board shows, for each player, how many known traits they fit.

nodes.title: guides/HOW_TO_PLAY Gathering, crafting, quests, creatures
nodes.text: Six resources grow at nodes in the forests, caves and camps. Hold E at a node to gather, and at a station to craft a Lantern, Crowbar, Lockpicks, Snare, Torch or Spade. Quest givers (the figures with a marker) trade resources for tools. Wolves and other creatures roam after dark and flee from light; a lit Lantern or Torch widens what you can see at night. GDD 3.14 to 3.16.

nodes.title: guides/HOW_TO_PLAY Winning
nodes.text: - **The village** wins by ejecting every Cabal member, by finishing the task bar, or by ejecting a Cabal member in the Final Night vote. - **The Cabal** wins at parity, or when the Final Night vote misses. - **The Drifter** wins alone by getting ejected, and the match goes on without them. Dead players become ghosts: they see every role, read the ghost channel, can finish their tasks and cast a non-binding "ghost suspect" shown on the end screen.

nodes.title: guides/HOW_TO_PLAY Tips for a first game
nodes.text: - Stay in pairs by day and compare Notebooks before the bell. - Report a body at once: an unreported body still forces a roll-call at dusk, later and with less to go on. - Sneak when you are near a house at night. Running makes noise others can hear and log. - Say where you were and with whom. A quiet player with no alibi gets voted out first. - Sound settings (music, effects, mute) are behind the gear on the landing page, the lobby and the HUD. The art style switch (8-bit or low poly) is on the landing page.

nodes.title: guides/QUICK_MODE Quick mode: One Night Ultimate Baguette
nodes.text: A short round for the same party: no walking, one night, one argument, one vote. The leader switches the mode chip in the lobby settings to **One Night Ultimate Baguette**. Timers, decks, stations and the winners table are in [`docs/GDD.md`](../GDD.md) 3.11.

nodes.title: guides/QUICK_MODE The fiction
nodes.text: Paris, the graveyard shift before the Bake-Off. You are bakers keeping the Mother Dough alive through the night. Hidden among you are Team Mold, who want it ruined. Nobody leaves the kitchen and nobody dies in the night: at dawn you argue, then one of you goes into the brick oven.

nodes.title: guides/QUICK_MODE Two cards each
nodes.text: - Your **Role card** says who you were dealt. - Your **Location card** is the prep station you choose to work at. - The **Pantry** in the middle of the table holds a few spare Role and Location cards. Cards move during the night. **You play for the team of the Role card in front of you at dawn**, not the one you were dealt. After the night nobody may look at their own cards, so the screen shows only what you remember: what you were dealt, where you worked, and what your own night act showed you.

nodes.title: guides/QUICK_MODE The phases
nodes.text: 1. **Role card.** Read it. Press Ready. Nobody sees who is ready. 2. **Evening Prep.** Pick a station, play its mini-game, and play one Ingredient card into its pile. Prep ends early when everyone has committed. 3. **The crime scenes.** Every pile is shuffled and flipped. Flags, net weight and any ruin are announced to all. 4. **The Baking Cycle.** The roles wake one by one in the order the deck sets and tamper with the cards: peek, swap, move a Pantry card. When it is your turn you get a short window and a screen to act on. 5. **Dawn.** The Iron Cloche is shown. 6. **Morning Rush.** Everyone…

nodes.title: guides/QUICK_MODE Winning
nodes.text: - **Loyal Bakers** win when at least one Mold Spore goes in the oven. If every Spore sits in the Pantry, they win by leaving the oven empty or baking a Team Mold card. - **Team Mold** wins when the Mother Dough is ruined at prep, or when no Spore goes in the oven. - **Le Croissant Rassis** plays alone and wins by going in the oven.

nodes.title: guides/QUICK_MODE Tips
nodes.text: - Say what you saw at night, but remember your card may have moved after you looked. - Watch the prep reveal: a ruined pile points at whoever worked that station. - A player who claims a role nobody else contests is probably telling the truth. Two players claiming the same role cannot both be.

nodes.text: Engine line. The plan pins Phaser 3.90.0 as decided and uses no 4-only features. Phaser 4.2.1 is now the maintained line and the official guidance is to start new projects on it; the switch costs about one M0 day (lighting and tint API names differ) and nothing else in this plan changes. Keep 3.90.0 or move to 4.2.1? Resolved 2026-10-10: Phaser 4.2.1 (A5). Confirmed 2026-10-10 (round 3).

nodes.text: Quick mode length. With the timers in balance.onub.json a match runs about 5-7 minutes, under the 6-9 minute target of GDD.md 3.11. nodes.text: Calibration sheet. Look at apps/client/public/assets/calibration/calibration_sheet.png and confirm A9 (key light 225°, die in 256 px cells) or ask for a re-render. Resolved 2026-10-10: A9 confirmed, with a re-render after a ramp fix (A25).

nodes.title: Open question 15: NPC fill policy (A16, GDD 3.12). Recommended: fill to 4 automatically, leader may add NPCs
nodes.text: NPC fill policy (A16, GDD 3.12). Recommended: fill to 4 automatically, leader may add NPCs up to 6 players, NPCs can hold any role including Killer with the scripted behaviour in 3.12, NPC matches count as practice. The simpler alternative is Village-only NPCs, which makes a 2-human party trivial (the Detective knows the other human is the Killer). Approve the recommendation, or choose Village-only? Resolved 2026-10-10: any role, fill to 4, leader up to 10, hidden NPC seats, three difficulty levels (A26).

meta.effect: Hold E to drag at reduced speed; dropping it into a body spot hides it; leaves a drag smear.

meta.name: Plant Clue
meta.effect: Places a footprint trail or a thread with the traits you choose. Inspect marks it Forged.

meta.name: Crowbar
meta.effect: Breaks a locked door; the door stays broken.

meta.name: Inherit
meta.effect: When the last Killer dies or is ejected the Knife passes to you with a longer kill cooldown; your Hunger clock starts in the round you inherit.

meta.name: Inspect
meta.effect: Reveals a clue's hidden attribute, exposes forgeries and marks it Verified. A dropped Magnifier lets anyone Inspect, slower.

meta.name: Dust / Compare
meta.effect: Dust lifts a print (limited charges); Compare any two prints: Match / No match. Never gives a name.

meta.name: Bandage
meta.effect: Not self. The target survives the next kill attempt within the window; both are knocked back, the target's screen blacks out and gets the attacker's height as Claimed; witnesses get height + scarf as Claimed; the attacker still gains Blood.

meta.name: Autopsy
meta.effect: Posts time of death (within the error) and cause (knife / wolf / poison / shot) as Verified.

meta.name: Salts
meta.effect: Cures Wounded or Snared.

meta.name: Lock / Unlock
meta.effect: Locks or unlocks any house door instantly. Locks keep people out, never in.

meta.name: Ledger
meta.effect: At each meeting, privately lists for each living player the last house they entered this cycle (house only, no time).

meta.name: Silent hide
meta.effect: Hide instantly and without noise; crawlspaces fit only you and adults cannot Check them.

meta.name: Witness
meta.effect: With line of sight to a kill within range, "The Child saw it" posts the killer's height + scarf as Verified at the next meeting.

meta.name: Slingshot
meta.effect: Stuns a player briefly.

meta.name: Tasks
meta.effect: Your chores fill the village bar; each one writes a Claimed alibi entry (time + scene).

meta.name: Chalk
meta.effect: Draws a floor mark visible to everyone.

meta.name: Rope
meta.effect: Frees a snared player.

meta.name: Act Shifty
meta.effect: Emits fake noise rings where you stand.

meta.name: Fake Blood
meta.effect: Shows Blood on your sprite in the world (meetings show portraits).

meta.name: Shoot
meta.effect: Kills a wolf.

meta.name: Arrest
meta.effect: Cuffs the target and drags them to the square; the next meeting opens with them as a Case Closed suspect.

meta.name: Snare
meta.effect: Holds whoever steps in and logs the name.

meta.name: Pickpocket
meta.effect: Takes one item from a player.

meta.name: Lockpick
meta.effect: Opens a locked door.

meta.name: Smoke
meta.effect: A smoke cloud blocks sight.

meta.name: Seance
meta.effect: The ghost picks 1 of 8 phrases.

meta.name: Skeleton Key
meta.effect: Opens any locked door and leaves a print on it.

meta.name: Clean
meta.effect: Erases one clue.

meta.name: Wash
meta.effect: Washes Blood off at the well or a basin and leaves a Wet Bucket clue.

meta.name: Medkit
meta.effect: Heals 1 HP.

meta.name: Light
meta.effect: Toggles a carried light; wolves flee it, but off is stealthier.

meta.name: Collect
meta.effect: Stand on a clue and hold E: it enters the Notebook with trait, scene and time.

meta.name: Report body
meta.effect: Starts a meeting; everyone moves to the square; the body stays.

meta.name: Emergency Bell
meta.effect: Rings the bell on the square to call a meeting; pulls per match come from the role.

meta.name: Hide
meta.effect: Enter a free hiding spot; you see a slit view and keep one action, Burst Out.

meta.name: Check
meta.effect: Opens a spot; checking an occupied spot writes a Verified entry for the hider naming you and the time.

meta.name: Burst Out
meta.effect: Leave a spot instantly, stunning whoever is Checking it.

meta.name: Sneak
meta.effect: Shift: silent footsteps at reduced speed.

meta.name: Impersonate
meta.effect: Your character shows a living seat's name, look, scarf and hat glyph at your own height for balance.json impersonate.durationS. The face changes only unseen: at once if no other living seat is in your scene, otherwise at your next door; ca…

meta.name: Hear Confession
meta.effect: Your Notebook gets the seat's faction (Village, Cabal or Neutral) as Verified. Not self.

meta.name: Keep Watch
meta.effect: The seat survives the first Knife strike before the night ends; the strike fails as on a Bandaged target and your Notebook records it. Not self, and not the seat you watched the night before (balance.json nightPowers.watchRepeatAllowed).

meta.name: Remedy
meta.effect: The seat survives the first Knife strike before the next meeting opens; your Notebook records it when it holds. It does not stop Nightshade or a shot.

meta.name: Nightshade
meta.effect: The seat dies when the night ends, a meeting opens or the Final Night hunt ends, wherever it stands; its body lies there with no trait clue. Not self.

meta.name: Last Shot
meta.effect: When you are killed, poisoned or ejected you may pick one living seat within the aim time, before you learn any role; it dies too. Accepted only while you aim. Not self.

meta.name: Pure Dairy
meta.effect: none
meta.text: Cold butter and fresh milk, straight off the frosted shelf.

meta.name: Active Yeast
meta.effect: none
meta.text: Wild yeast, harvested and bubbling.

meta.name: Spoiled Milk
meta.effect: none
meta.text: It smelled fine in the dark.

meta.name: Unpasteurized Mold
meta.effect: none
meta.text: A green bloom in the cream.

meta.name: Thermostat Flip
meta.effect: discardRandomOther
meta.text: Flip the switch. One other card in this pile thaws away unseen.

meta.name: T55 Flour
meta.effect: none
meta.text: A heavy sack of farine, sifted fine.

meta.name: Sea Salt
meta.effect: none
meta.text: Grey salt from the coast, measured true.

meta.name: Sawdust
meta.effect: none
meta.text: It is almost the same colour.

meta.name: Plaster
meta.effect: none
meta.text: A scoop from the cracked wall.

meta.name: Floor Sweepings
meta.effect: none
meta.text: Whatever was under the bench.

meta.name: Warm Steam
meta.effect: none
meta.text: The glass fogs and the dough rises.

meta.name: Time
meta.effect: none
meta.text: Leave it alone. It knows what to do.

meta.name: Cold Draft
meta.effect: none
meta.text: Prop the cabinet door open a crack.

meta.name: Over-Proofing
meta.effect: none
meta.text: Just a little longer. Then a little longer.

meta.name: Oak Firewood
meta.effect: none
meta.text: Dry oak, split thin, for a fierce clean heat.

meta.name: Steam Injection
meta.effect: none
meta.text: The coup de buée: one burst of steam for the crust.

meta.name: Charcoal Ash
meta.effect: none
meta.text: Smothers the flame from underneath.

meta.name: Wet Wood
meta.effect: none
meta.text: Hisses, smokes and never catches.

meta.effect: cloche
meta.description: Put the Iron Cloche on one player's Role or Location card, your own included; nobody else can peek at or swap it tonight.

meta.effect: peek
meta.description: Peek at one Pantry Role card.

meta.effect: peek
meta.description: Peek at one other player's Location card.

meta.effect: swapWithOwn
meta.description: Swap your Location card with a Pantry Location card or another player's; you see the one you now hold.

meta.effect: peek
meta.description: Peek at one other player's Role card.

meta.effect: peek
meta.description: Peek at two Pantry Role cards.

meta.effect: peek
meta.description: Look at two other players' Location cards.

meta.effect: swapWithOwn
meta.description: Swap your Role card with another player's and look at your new card.

meta.effect: peek
meta.description: Look at one Pantry Role card; you must then swap it into the line.

meta.effect: swapWithPeeked
meta.description: Swap the Pantry card you looked at with any player's Role card, your own included.

meta.effect: swapWithOwn
meta.description: Swap your Role card with a Pantry Role card without looking.

meta.effect: swapPair
meta.description: Swap two other players' Role cards without looking.

meta.effect: swapPair
meta.description: Swap two other players' Location cards without looking.

meta.effect: peek
meta.description: Look at your own Role and Location cards.

meta.text: The Stale Croissant and a Mold Spore both went in the oven and the dough held: the Croissant and the Loyal Bakers win.
The Stale Croissant went in the oven: it wins alone, even over a ruined dough.
The Mother Dough was ruined at prep: Team Mold wins.
A Mold Spore went in the oven: the Loyal Bakers win.
No Mold Spore went in the oven: Team Mold wins, even those who were baked.
Every Mold Spore was in the Pantry and nobody went in the oven: the Loyal Bakers win.
No Spore was at the table and Team Mold went in the oven: the Loyal Bakers win.
No Spore was at the table but the oven took someone else: whoever holds a Team Mold card wins; if nobody does, nobody wins.

meta.name: Body
meta.description: Cause headline; reporting it starts a meeting; a hidden body screams again when its spot is Checked.

meta.name: Footprints
meta.description: A trail toward the exit; the stride spacing gives the height.

meta.name: Thread
meta.description: Snagged on a door or furniture; the colour gives the scarf.

meta.name: Snagged felt
meta.description: On the exit door frame; the Detective's Dust reads the hat.

meta.name: Blood
meta.description: On the killer's sprite, visible within range; washed off at the well or a basin.

meta.name: Wet Bucket
meta.description: Left where someone washed Blood off.

meta.name: Fingerprint
meta.description: The last touchers of doors, items and bodies, kept server-side; Compare gives Match / No match.

meta.name: Drag smear
meta.description: A trail from the kill tile to the body spot; Verified when Inspected.

meta.name: Time of death
meta.description: From an Autopsy, within the error window.

meta.name: Silhouette
meta.description: "The Child saw it": height and scarf.

meta.name: Ledger
meta.description: The last house each living player entered this cycle.

meta.name: Dropped items
meta.description: The dead player's inventory, except role-bound items.

meta.name: Fur
meta.description: Wolf kills leave fur, never footprints.

meta.name: Claw marks
meta.description: Wolf kills leave claw marks.

meta.name: Drip trail
meta.description: A Wounded player leaves drips while Wounded.

meta.name: Glowing footprints
meta.description: A Hungry Killer leaves a glowing footprint showing their own height on the tiles they cross, until they strike.

meta.name: Landing footprints
meta.description: A one-way drop leaves a footprint trail at the landing.

meta.name: Long-stride footprints
meta.description: The grace-phase teaching clue beside the well: "Footprints, long stride: Tall".

meta.name: Skeleton Key
meta.tooltip: Open any locked door; leaves a print.

meta.name: Crowbar
meta.tooltip: Break a locked door; it stays broken.

meta.name: Notebook
meta.tooltip: Auto-logs what you collect and learn.

meta.name: Bandage
meta.tooltip: The target survives the next kill attempt.

meta.name: Lantern
meta.tooltip: Carried light; wolves flee it. Off is stealthier.

meta.name: Candle
meta.tooltip: Small carried light; wolves flee it.

meta.name: Replica Knife
meta.tooltip: Looks like a knife. It is not.

meta.name: Snare
meta.tooltip: Holds a player who steps in.

meta.name: Torch
meta.tooltip: Carried light, crafted from timber and resin; wolves flee it.

meta.name: Study Key
meta.tooltip: Opens the locked study in Vane Manor.

meta.name: Seance Chalk
meta.tooltip: Hold a seance at a body.

meta.name: Remedy
meta.tooltip: One seat survives the next knife before the next meeting.

meta.name: Nightshade
meta.tooltip: One seat dies when the night ends.

meta.name: Fowling Piece
meta.tooltip: Your last shot, when you fall.

meta.name: Spade
meta.tooltip: Dig tin ore out of a seam.

meta.name: Tin Ore
meta.tooltip: Crafting: lanterns, lockpicks, crowbars. Needs a spade.

meta.name: Herbs
meta.tooltip: Crafting: snares; wanted by quest givers.

meta.name: the Detective
meta.silhouette: Belted trench coat with the collar up and a snap-brim fedora, a lens raised in one hand.
meta.notes: The outsider from the mainland, cleaner and sharper than the villagers: a fog trench coat belted tight, ink fedora and gloves, the magnifier's lens the accent (a lantern glint). Interact: crouches with the lens to the ground.

meta.name: the Doctor
meta.silhouette: Short top hat and a long frock coat, a squat bag carried low: narrow on top, heavy at one hand.
meta.notes: Ink frock coat over a bone waistcoat and shirt, round spectacles, a short ink top hat, the black medical bag with a mustard clasp, a watch chain. Interact: kneels and opens the bag.

meta.name: the Vicar
meta.silhouette: Wide shovel-brimmed hat over an ankle-length cassock: a dark bell shape with a pale collar.
meta.notes: Black cassock to the boots, white collar band and cuffs, a small prayer book at the chest (bone pages, mustard clasp). The brim must read from all 8 directions; keep the cassock one dark mass so the scarf stands out. Interact: reads from t…

meta.name: the Watchman
meta.silhouette: Tall domed helmet and a shoulder-caped greatcoat, a pole lantern held up beside him: the one look with a light above the head.
meta.notes: Knee-length slate greatcoat with a short fog shoulder cape, a high stiff collar under the scarf, a domed watchman's helmet, a wooden rattle on the belt. The pole lantern's glass is the accent and glows in every frame; the whole figure stay…

meta.name: the Herbalist
meta.silhouette: Deep hood up and a wide pocketed apron hung with bundles: a hunched, layered shape.
meta.notes: A hooded fog shawl over a bone apron with many pockets, dried herb bundles and a satchel at the hip (dried fog and bone tones, never teal), two small vial stoppers in mustard. The hood is the headgear. Interact: grinds in a mortar held at …

meta.name: the Gamekeeper
meta.silhouette: A long gun slung barrel-up over one shoulder and a deerstalker: the one diagonal line above a shoulder.
meta.notes: Slate tweed shooting coat with a fog check, breeches and gaiters, a deerstalker with the flaps tied up, a game bag across the body, the fowling piece slung barrel-up (ink barrel, mustard brass). Interact: kneels and checks a snare.

meta.name: the Lamplighter
meta.silhouette: Bare head and a short hooded oilskin cape, a long lighting pole at a slant over the shoulder with a flame at its tip.
meta.notes: Short slate oilskin cape with the hood down, bone shirt with the sleeves rolled, a brass-hooked lighting pole carried at a slant inside the 1.75-tile silhouette, its small flame the accent. Interact: raises the pole to an unseen lamp.

meta.name: the Baker
meta.silhouette: Tall pleated toque and a long white apron: the one pale figure.
meta.notes: Bone toque and apron over a fog shirt and trousers, sleeves rolled, flour on the forearms, a long wooden peel or a basket of loaves (mustard crust). The pale base is deliberate, so the Baker reads at night; keep the scarf a clear band agai…

meta.name: the Fisher
meta.silhouette: Sou'wester sloping down at the back, a knee-length smock and tall boots, a coil of net over one shoulder.
meta.notes: Fog oilskin smock, ink sea boots to the knee, the sou'wester in mustard (the accent; keep it small), a coil of net and a cork float over the shoulder. Interact: mends a net held in both hands.

meta.name: the Tinner
meta.silhouette: A hard round hat with a lit candle pressed to the front, a leather jerkin and a short pick on the shoulder.
meta.notes: Hard felt tinner's hat with a candle stuck in a clay lump at the front (its flame the accent), slate leather jerkin, fog shirt, rolled trousers with ore dust at the knees, a short pick over the shoulder. Fits Hollowmere's shut tin mine and…

meta.name: the Killer
meta.silhouette: Portrait only: a long coat and a brim that keeps the face in shadow, a knife held low behind the back.
meta.notes: Never made, rendered or packed as a world character. The face stays unreadable (no eyes, a lantern rim light on the jaw); the blade's edge is the only blood. Nothing in it may echo a world look, so no portrait hints at a cover.

meta.name: the Accomplice
meta.silhouette: Portrait only: half turned away, a crowbar under the arm and a spool of red thread in the hand.
meta.notes: Never a world character. A forger's shape: ink-stained cuffs, a footprint stencil tucked in the coat, the thread spool in blood, the face half lit.

meta.name: the Drifter
meta.silhouette: Portrait only: a patched travelling coat, a bindle and a grin, a wooden knife in the belt.
meta.notes: Never a world character. Neutral amber: mustard patches and bindle cloth, the replica knife plainly wooden. Looks like trouble on purpose.

scalars.name: Blackpine
scalars.blurb: Storm-cut logging camp: bunkhouse, sawmill, pine woods and the company's tin workings under the hill.

scalars.name: Hollowmere
scalars.blurb: Fog-bound harbour hamlet: lanes, a tavern and a manor, two woods and Vane's flooded tin gallery.

meta.name: Killer
meta.goal: Kill until the Cabal matches the village (one villager left at 4-5), and never get voted out.
meta.win: Parity at 6+ players, living Village at most 1 at 4-5, or the Final Night vote fails.
meta.cardText: Walk in a borrowed character. Strike after dark when the room is empty, clean one clue, wash at the well, then be the loudest voice asking who did it.
meta.beware: Clues match your own traits whatever face you wear; your height never changes; Blood shows within 3 tiles; a guarded target voids your kill.

meta.name: Accomplice
meta.goal: Cover for the Killer and take the knife if they fall.
meta.cardText: You never hold the knife, only the alibi. Forge trails, break the right doors, vouch at the right moment.
meta.beware: Inspect marks plants Forged; a Forged entry tells the village an Accomplice exists; your cover is a claim someone may test.

meta.name: Accomplice, Knife-bearer
meta.goal: Carry on the Killer's work alone: strike after dark, keep your cover.
meta.cardText: The Knife has passed to you. The Killer is gone and the village does not know it yet; finish what they started.
meta.beware: Your Hunger clock starts in the round you inherit; your cover is still a claim someone may test.

meta.name: Detective
meta.goal: Verify the clues that narrow the suspects.
meta.cardText: Collect, inspect, cross-reference. Your Verified clues narrow the board; the village does the rest.
meta.beware: Prime target; the Rag erases clues; forgeries cost Lenses; Compare never gives a name. If you die the Magnifier drops and anyone can Inspect in 6 s.

meta.name: Doctor
meta.goal: Keep people alive and read the dead.
meta.cardText: Keep people alive and read the dead. Your autopsy says when; that is what breaks alibis.
meta.beware: Two-Killer games outpace your bandages.

meta.name: Butler
meta.goal: Control the doors and say who went where.
meta.cardText: You know every door in Hollowmere. Control the wings, read the ledger, say who went where.
meta.beware: Universal access makes you the obvious suspect; Skeleton Key use looks like yours.

meta.name: Child
meta.goal: Hide, watch, and remember who you saw.
meta.cardText: You are small and quiet. Hide, watch, remember.
meta.beware: Top kill target; vision -1 tile; cannot pick up items.

meta.name: Townsfolk
meta.goal: Do your chores in pairs and vote with evidence.
meta.cardText: Do your chores with others to build alibis, mark what you see, vote with evidence.
meta.beware: Weak alone; strong in pairs.

meta.name: Drifter
meta.goal: Get yourself voted out.
meta.win: Get ejected (solo win; the match continues and the end screen lists you among the winners).
meta.cardText: You want to hang. Be suspicious enough to be voted out, not so obvious they ignore you.
meta.beware: A calm village; dying to the Killer is a loss; counts as nobody for parity; you wear a cover like the Cabal, but alone.

meta.name: Ranger
meta.goal: Hunt the wolves and make your one arrest count.
meta.cardText: You hunt wolves. One arrest per match: be right.
meta.beware: Bolts are loud (noise 10).

meta.name: Thief
meta.goal: Escape by the cave sea exit holding 3 Heirlooms.
meta.win: Escape by the cave sea exit holding 3 Heirlooms.
meta.cardText: Nobody's hero.
meta.beware: Thefts look like Killer activity; counts as Village for parity.

meta.name: Medium
meta.goal: Hear the dead.
meta.cardText: You hear the dead.
meta.beware: Cabal ghosts may lie.

meta.name: Vicar
meta.goal: Learn one soul's faction each night and steer the vote.
meta.cardText: Everyone in Hollowmere confesses to you sooner or later. Each night, learn where one soul stands, then choose how much to say.
meta.beware: Everyone can see you are the Vicar, the Cabal first among them; if your card was not dealt, a Cabal player may wear your face and lie in your name.

meta.name: Watchman
meta.goal: Stand guard over one neighbour each night.
meta.cardText: You walk the lanes after dark. Each night, choose one door to stand by; if a blade comes for that soul tonight, it fails.
meta.beware: You cannot watch yourself or the same soul two nights running; poison and the Gamekeeper's shot go past you.

meta.name: Herbalist
meta.goal: Save one life and end one, once each, and be right both times.
meta.cardText: One bottle saves, one bottle ends. Pour the first where the knife will fall and the second only where you are certain.
meta.beware: Nightshade kills a villager as readily as a killer, and a Remedy cannot stop it.

meta.name: Gamekeeper
meta.goal: If you fall, take the right one with you.
meta.cardText: Vane paid you to keep the wood. If they come for you, you will not go alone; make sure the one you take is the one who came.
meta.beware: You never see the blow that fells you, and the face that walked up may have been borrowed; a wasted shot kills a friend.

meta.name: Lamplighter
meta.goal: Do your chores in pairs and vote with evidence.
meta.cardText: You light the lanterns that keep the wolves off the square. Work beside others, mark what you see, vote with evidence.
meta.beware: Weak alone; strong in pairs.

meta.name: Baker
meta.goal: Do your chores in pairs and vote with evidence.
meta.cardText: Up before anyone, flour to the elbows. Do your chores in company, mark what you see, vote with evidence.
meta.beware: Weak alone; strong in pairs.

meta.name: Fisher
meta.goal: Do your chores in pairs and vote with evidence.
meta.cardText: The fog keeps the boats in. Mend the nets beside a neighbour, mark what you see, vote with evidence.
meta.beware: Weak alone; strong in pairs.

meta.name: Tinner
meta.goal: Do your chores in pairs and vote with evidence.
meta.cardText: The mine is shut; your hands are not. Work in pairs, mark what you see, vote with evidence.
meta.beware: Weak alone; strong in pairs.

scalars.cardLine: You play for the card in front of you at dawn, not the card you were dealt. Argue for who you think you are.

meta.name: Loyal Bakers
meta.goal: Put at least one Mold Spore in the oven. If every Spore is in the Pantry, keep the oven empty or bake Team Mold.

meta.name: Team Mold
meta.goal: Ruin the Mother Dough at prep, or keep every Mold Spore out of the oven.

meta.name: On your own
meta.goal: Get yourself put in the oven.

meta.name: Le Boulanger
meta.nightAct: Wake first. Put the Iron Cloche on any player's Role or Location card, your own included. Nobody can peek at or swap it tonight.
meta.cardText: Your dough, your bench, your cloche. Slam the Iron Cloche over the one card you trust; nothing touches it until dawn.

meta.name: Le Champignon
meta.nightAct: Wake with the other Spore and see each other. If you are the only Spore at the table, peek at one Pantry Role card.
meta.cardText: You crawled out from behind the damp bricks to ruin the Mother Dough. Ruin it at prep, or keep every Spore out of the oven.

meta.name: Le Levain
meta.nightAct: Wake after the Spores and see who was dealt Le Champignon. They do not know you.
meta.cardText: Your jar bubbles over to feed the spores. You know who they are and they do not know you: lie for them, even into the oven.

meta.name: L'Apprenti
meta.nightAct: Peek at one other player's Location card.
meta.cardText: Sixteen hours on a stool and nobody pays you. You read one line of the shift log; use it to cover for Team Mold, whoever they are.

meta.name: Le Rat de Cave
meta.nightAct: Swap your Location card with a Pantry Location card or with another player's. You see the one you now hold.
meta.cardText: You pry up the floor grate and leave flour prints in someone else's room. Trade your alibi for a better one.

meta.name: Le Commis
meta.nightAct: Wake with the other Commis and see each other. If you wake alone, the other Commis is in the Pantry.
meta.cardText: You chopped side by side all shift. Vouch for each other, unless the night moved one of you.

meta.name: Le Chef de Cuisine
meta.nightAct: Peek at one other player's Role card, or at two Pantry Role cards.
meta.cardText: Under the green banker's lamp you audit the personnel files. Find the rot before the bake.

meta.name: L'Aboyeur
meta.nightAct: Look at two other players' Location cards.
meta.cardText: The grainy green monitor shows every room. You know where two people really worked; catch the one lying about it.

meta.name: Le Sous-Chef
meta.nightAct: Swap your Role card with another player's and look at your new card.
meta.cardText: You ring the brass bell and reassign the staff. Whatever card you take is who you are now, even if it is mold.

meta.name: Le Tourrier
meta.nightAct: Look at one Pantry Role card, then swap it with any player's Role card, your own included. You must swap.
meta.cardText: You fold an unused recipe back into the line. Someone wakes up as somebody else, and only you know what went in.

meta.name: Le Plongeur
meta.nightAct: Swap two other players' Role cards, or two other players' Location cards, without looking.
meta.cardText: Soapsuds, steam and wet-floor cones: you put the pans back in the wrong places, and nobody, you included, knows which.

meta.name: Le Garde Manger
meta.nightAct: Swap your Role card with a Pantry Role card without looking. You must swap.
meta.cardText: One glass of cooking wine too many. You wandered off and came back wearing someone else's apron.

meta.name: L'Inspecteur Sanitaire
meta.nightAct: Wake last. Look at your own Role and Location cards.
meta.cardText: Clipboard, thermometer, UV torch: you make the last sweep before opening. You alone know what you hold at dawn.

meta.name: Le Croissant Rassis
meta.nightAct: No night act. You win alone if you are put in the oven.
meta.cardText: Hard as a rock under the display-case spotlight, you pray for the oven. Act just guilty enough; if they bake you, you win alone.

meta.name: Le Critique Gastronomique
meta.nightAct: No night act. If you are put in the oven, the player you voted for goes in with you.
meta.cardText: Behind the velvet rope with an empty plate and a fountain pen, you judge the kitchen. If they bake you by mistake, your pen drags your vote in with you.

scalars.name: Apothecary loft
scalars.notes: Near-dark, one green lamp.

scalars.name: Mallory Apothecary
scalars.notes: Basin (Blood wash); Wrench on the bench; the NOT FOR SALE shelf with one empty slot.

scalars.name: Crumb's Ovens
scalars.notes: Wake Table with up to 10 named plates, oven ledge with the dead's three loaves, the Baker's ledger, cold oven, flour floor. Hub of the quick mode (GDD 3.11); in the main match a task node (Fetch the flour) and a Blood-wash basin.

scalars.name: Hale Barn
scalars.notes: Goat bleats when anyone enters; wolf pelt on the door.

scalars.name: Blackpine Camp
scalars.notes: Blackpine's hub. Hill and adit north with tram rails to the ore bin, the pine line and woods trail west, the Blackwater and the broken trestle south, the log pond and flume east. The yard holds the shift bell, the pump and teaching clue, t…

scalars.name: Company Office
scalars.notes: Two rooms split by a wall. Company store: counter with a hiding spot behind it, empty shelves. Manager's office: payroll ledger open at a torn page, the safe, the map table, the dead telephone, a wardrobe, the strongroom door (body spot). …

scalars.name: The Flooded Gallery

scalars.name: The Undercroft
scalars.notes: Pitch dark with a small ambient radius; gas pockets in marked side alcoves (V1.5).

scalars.name: St Brannock's
scalars.notes: Silent zone: no footstep noise. The bell rope with a torn glove in it is decoration.

scalars.styleFormula: Art style: the isometric pixel-art cutaway dioramas of the reference images. Chunky visible pixels on a strict grid, crisp one-pixel near-black outlines, flat three-tone cel shading with a few hand-placed highlight pixels, small dither pat…
scalars.styleToken: isometric pixel-art cutaway diorama, 1px dark outlines, 3-tone cel, warm lamplight vs cold blue, dense props, no text
scalars.styleAvoid: Avoid: photorealism, a 3D-render look, smooth gradients, soft airbrush, lens blur, depth of field, bloom haze, painterly brush strokes, flat vector art, anime or chibi proportions, a perspective camera, legible signage or lettering.

nodes.title: cs.hollowmere.title
nodes.text: HOLLOWMERE — EST. BY THE RAILROAD EXPANSE

nodes.title: cs.hollowmere.seven
nodes.text: Seven days' walk from the nearest soul, hemmed in by black pines and freezing mud.

nodes.title: cs.hollowmere.laid
nodes.text: It was laid down, tie by tie and spike by spike, by the Railroad Barons.

nodes.title: cs.hollowmere.own
nodes.text: They own the mill. They own the bank. They own the dirt under your boots.

nodes.title: cs.hollowmere.train
nodes.text: And if you ever hope to leave, you wait for the train.

nodes.title: cs.hollowmere.dusk
nodes.text: Folks lock their doors at dusk and tip their hats to the Detective.

nodes.title: cs.hollowmere.end
nodes.text: Nobody comes to the end of the line unless they're running from something, or hunting it.

nodes.title: cs.hollowmere.vicar
nodes.text: A new Vicar stepped off the platform. Someone is already measuring him for a coffin.

nodes.title: cs.hollowmere.letter
nodes.text: Somewhere in today's mailbag, a sealed letter offers one of you a fortune to kill.

nodes.title: cs.hollowmere.nobody
nodes.text: In HollowMere, nobody kills for nothing. Everyone has a price, a prayer, or a vendetta.

nodes.title: cs.hollowmere.check
nodes.text: Check your pockets. Read your mail. Watch the shadows.

nodes.title: cs.hollowmere.miss
nodes.text: And whatever you do, don't miss the train.

nodes.title: cs.deathKnife.line
nodes.text: A cold edge, and the lantern goes out.

nodes.title: cs.deathPoison.line
nodes.text: Something in the cup was not sugar.

nodes.title: cs.deathShot.line
nodes.text: One shot, and the whole square goes quiet.

nodes.title: cs.deathEjected.line
nodes.text: The town has spoken.

nodes.title: cs.deathWolf.line
nodes.text: The pines were not empty.
